content.title: 2026 Masters live leaderboard updates, Round 3 tee times, TV coverage
content.text: Updated April 11, 2026, 7:03 p.m. ETThe Masters continues from Augusta National Golf Club with Moving Day. The Saturday Round 3 has always carried a surprise or two, and maybe even someone overtaking the lead.But if that happens this year, it may be the biggest surprise of them all.That's because Rory McIlroy has a lead so big, no player in Masters history has been this far ahead after 36 holes. His six-shot advantage will be what everyone is watching on Saturday, especially when he and Sam Burns are last to tee off on Saturday at 2:50 p.m.Watch the Masters live on Fubo (free trial) Masters leaderboardT1. Scottie Scheffler: -7 (F)T9. 4 tied at -6Keep up with all the latest scores on our live Masters leaderboard.Masters coverage today: Where to watch on TV, live streamNoon-2 p.m.: Paramount+2-7 p.m.: CBSStreaming: ESPN app | Fubo (free trial) | Masters.com and the Masters appRound 3 of the 2026 Masters will broadcast nationally on Paramount+, CBS' subscription streaming servce, starting at noon before switching to CBS at 2 p.m. The CBS broadcast is available to stream via Fubo, which offers a free trial for new subscribers, and the tournament is available to stream for free on Masters.com and the Masters app. Featured group and hole streaming from PGA Tour Live is available on the ESPN app (with a subscription to the Select plan) starting at 10:15 a.m. Rory McIlroy score today at the MastersLeading by six strokes to start the day, defending champ Rory McIlroy ran into trouble in Round 3. He drove his first two tee shots into the rough to see the lead shrink early, then after treading water for most of the day, McIlroy hit into trouble on Amen Corner, hitting into water on No. 11 for a double bogey and finding the rough on Nos. 12 and 13. Cameron Young overtook him for the lead before McIlroy responded with a birdie on 14 to climb back atop the pack with Young. Follow McIlroy's round live with our updating Rory tracker. Rory McIlroy drops a shot, tied with Cameron YoungRory McIlroy's regained lead was short-lived, as he had to scramble to give himself a chance at par on the par-4 17th. But McIlroy's birdie putt stopped short a few inches from the hole, forcing him to settle for a bogey to fall back into a tie with Cameron Young at 11 under. Rory McIlroy retakes the lead, all alone, at the MastersSee, nothing to worry about, right? Rory McIlroy carried the momentum of the birdie on Hole 14 to the next challenge, the par-5 15th. There, he reached the green in two, then made a real go at an eagle attempt. It fell just a few inches short, but his birdie put him back at 12 under for the tournament and all alone in the lead. Rory McIlroy responds with a birdie for a share of the lead at 2026 MastersThe wheels appeared to be falling off for Rory McIlory, who was 2 over through 13 holes and watched his six-shot lead turn into a one-shot deficit. But, he buckled down and made a 3 on the par-4 14th, thanks for a nifty birdie putt of about 20 feet. He and Cameron Young, who finished his third round with a 7-under 65, are tied at 11 under for the tournament. Cameron Young takes Masters leadHe came into the day eight shots back, but Players Championship winner Cameron Young has overtaken Rory McIlroy for the Masters lead. Young drained a 27-footer for birdie on the 16th, and after Rory McIlroy once again hit into the rough on No. 12, there's a change atop the leaderboard. Young is back to 7 under on the day and is 11 under for the tournament. Rory McIlroy finds waterUh-oh. Rory McIlroy's second shot on the par-4 11th took a few big, juicy bounces in front of the green and rolled right into the water. He settled for double bogey and is back to just one shot clear of Cameron Young at 11 under. Jason Day goes on a birdie run at the MastersIt's been a day for wild runs at Augusta. Jason Day, who has three top-5 finishes at the Masters to his name, rocketed up the leaderboard with four straight birdies from Nos. 12-15. The Australian finds himself at 5 under on the day and 9 under for the tournament. Cameron Young cools off after finding waterCameron Young is now one behind Rory McIlroy. The Players champion got a little lucky on the 13th with a favorable bounce that put him back on the fairway, and he nearly converted it into an eagle. Instead he went back-to-back birdies on Nos. 13 and 14 to briefly find himself just behind the leader.But on No. 15, Young's third shot couldn't make it onto the green, and the ball slowly gained speed as it rolled down the hill and into the water. He managed to scrape together a bogey on the hole, falling back to 10 under and three behind the lead. He got another break though: McIlroy also hit into the water on No. 11. Haotong Li challenging Rory McIlroyHe made a stunning run to the top-5 at the 2025 British Open, and now Haotong Li is making his presence felt at the Masters. The 30-year-old from China sank an eagle on the par-5 eighth hole to drop to 5 under on the day and 9 under for the tournament, tying him for third three strokes back. He ran into trouble on No. 13, however, after getting aggressive on his approach and hitting into the water in front of the green. Rory McIlroy skipping RBC HeritageHe's in the lead at the Masters, but don't expect to see Rory McIlroy at the RBC Heritage next week. The field for the signature event in Hilton Head, South Carolina does not include the world No. 2, though Scottie Scheffler and other big names will be there. Scottie Scheffler birdie shakes Rory McIlroyWorld No. 1 Scottie Scheffler stuck his tee shot on the par-3 16th perfectly to within 10 feet of the cup. After sinking his birdie putt to fall to 7 under, Rory McIlroy was about to tee off on the nearby sixth when the crowd roared, causing him to step back. The leader's tee shot sailed well left of the green and rolled for a while among the patrons. However, McIlroy was able to save par.Scheffler ran into trouble hitting into the vegetation on the 18th, but he nearly scratched out a birdie on his approach shot, finishing his 7-under round of 65 with a par. He heads into the final round at 7 under for the tournament, within shouting distance of the lead (for now, at least). Cameron Young charging at MastersCount Players Championship winner Cameron Young among those off to strong starts in Round 3. The 28-year-old put up back-to-back birdies on holes 3 and 4, then again on Nos. 7 and 8. Young got another one on the 10th, putting him at 9 under for the tournament, tied with Haotong Li for second just three shots behind Rory McIlroy. Collin Morikawa holes outHe might be farther behind the pack for now, but Collin Morikawa is on a nice run after Amen Corner. The two-time major champion saw his 92-yard approach on No. 15 bounce a few times, then gently roll back into the cup for an eagle. Morikawa followed with birdies on the 16th and 17th to fall to 5 under for the tournament. Patrick Cantlay finishes bogey-free round at MastersPatrick Cantlay's birdie on the 18th closed the book on an excellent day for the 34-year-old, who made four of his six birdies on the back nine to finish at 6 under for the day and the tournament. He heads to the clubhouse in the top 10. Shane Lowry hole-in-one at the Masters!For the first time since 2022, we have an ace at the Masters! Shane Lowry, who also drained a hole-in-one at Augusta in 2016, jumped for joy after watching his ball roll into the sixth hole. The roar from the crowd was so loud, Harris English had to stop on the nearby 16th green to acknowledge it.Lowry now sits in a tie for second at 8 under, four shots behind his good friend Rory McIlroy. Patrick Reed, Sam Burns on fire to start the MastersRory McIlroy might have sent his first two drives into the rough, but both players tied for second entering the day are hot on his trail. 2018 champion Patrick Reed opened his round with three straight birdies to rocket up to 9 under par, while Burns, McIlroy's partner for Round 3, drained birdies on holes 1 and 2. Wyndham Clark nearly hits ace on par-4Wyndham Clark came a few feet from the first hole-in-one of the 2026 Masters ... and it was at the par-4 third! Clark's 5-foot eagle putt got him to 3 under for Round 3 today and 6 under for the tournament. Ludvig Åberg, Hideki Matsuyama, Haotong Li making runs at the MastersScottie Scheffler's not the only one putting the pressure on Rory McIlroy. 2023 runner-up Ludvig Åberg started his back nine with three straight birdies to get him to 2 under for the tournament. Farther up the leaderboard, Hideki Matsuyama birdied holes 3-5 to put him at 5 under, while Haotong Li started with three birds in a row to climb into a tie for third at 6 under. Scottie Scheffler nearly holes-out for eagle on 9 to continue hot streakIt would take a Herculian effort to catch Rory McIlroy, but the World's No. 1 player and the man who slipped the Green Jacket on McIlroy last year may be up to the challenge. Scottie Scheffler's second shot on the par-4 ninth lipped out for a near eagle. He did complete the hole with a birdie for a 5 under in the front nine in today's Round 3, and another one on No. 11 has him at 6 under for the tournament. Chris Gotterup moves up leaderboard with eagleA little more than an hour after Scottie Scheffler eagled the second hole, Chris Gotterup got into that action with an eagle of his own. The two-time winner on the PGA Tour this year climbed up into the top five at 5 under, seven strokes behind leader Rory McIlroy. Scottie Scheffler eagles early at the MastersTwo-time Masters champion Scottie Scheffler, the betting favorite entering the 2026 Masters, enters the weekend at just even par after shooting a 2-over 74 on Friday. He teed off tied for 26th and 12 shots behind the lead, but an eagle on No. 2 has him on the right path. The world No. 1 blasted a perfect second shot 265 yards to within 6 feet of the hole. Scheffler had a shot at a birdie on the third, but he missed a 7-foot putt to the left. Back-to-back birdies on Nos. 7 and 8 got him to 4 under and into the top 10. Low scores at Masters todayOf the 37 players to have teed off so far in Round 3, only four are over par for the day, and Ben Griffin just bogeyed the first hole. Eight players are at even, so expect scores to drop today when Rory McIlroy and the leaders hit the course. Has there been a hole-in-one at the Masters 2026?While there were four aces at the Par 3 Contest on Wednesday, the official Masters Tournament has yet to see a hole-in-one this year. We almost got one yesterday from 18-year-old amateur Mason Howell on No. 12, but the ball came a few feet short. There hasn't been an ace at the Masters since Stewart Cink dropped one in on No. 16 with an 8-iron. Masters purse 2026: What is payout for Masters winner?The Masters announced its prize money for 2026 shortly after noon Saturday, and to no surprise, it's a doozy. The total purse is a record $22.5 million, with the winner taking $4.5 million and the runner-up "settling" for $2.43 million. Take a look at the full payout breakdown. Brian Harman continues hot streak after surviving Masters cutIt wasn't looking good for Georgia native Brian Harman early in the second round, with a double bogey on No. 4 putting him at 10 over par for the tournament. But he ramped into high gear after that with four straight birdies, part of seven on the day, allowing him to hit the 4-over cut line. Harman has continued that success into Round 3 with birdies on the second, fourth and sixth holes. He is 9 under par over his last 20 holes at Augusta. Bryson DeChambeau, Robert MacIntyre among the cutsJon Rahm narrowly avoided the 4-over cut line and will play the weekend at Augusta National. Some prominent players who missed the cut include Bryson DeChambeau, who triple-bogeyed the 18th hole. Robert MacIntyre missed out as well, and he posted an AI-generated image of himself as one of Augusta's trademark gnomes giving the middle finger, a reference to his flipping off the 15th green in the Round 1. What is Amen Corner?Golf journalist Herbert Warren Wind coined the phrase "Amen Corner" in a legendary Sports Illustrated article published on April 21, 1958 when he recapped the Masters Tournament won by Arnold Palmer. Amen Corner is the approach shot to the par-4 11th hole, the par-3 12th, and the tee shot at the par-5 13th hole. It's at the lowest level of the hilly golf course co-designed by club founder Bobby Jones and Alister MacKenzie and the amphitheater setting behind the 12th tee, with huge bleachers and thousands of patrons, has been the site for numerous Masters dramas since the tournament began in 1934.Florida Times-Union golf reporter Garry Smits takes a walk through the storied history of Amen Corner.Masters favorites to winLatest odds according to BetMGM:Rory McIlroy: +200Patrick Reed: +650Justin Rose: +800Tommy Fleetwood: +900Xander Schauffele: +1400Jason Day: +1400 Sign Up Bonus Bet $5 Get $250 If Your Bet Wins!
